scenes.credit: Google's launch film, from @GoogleAI's post on X

steps.say: Google's launch film for Gemini 4 Neon. An agent swarm pulls old photographs of King's College.

steps.caption: a demo Google chose, not a benchmark
steps.say: Then it models Alan Turing's study in Blender, and renders it. Google says the run took twelve hours.

scenes.headline: The model below Carbon that outscores it
scenes.sub: Gemini 4 Neon, checked against the leaderboards
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ignis. Google says Neon sits between Carbon and Hydrogen. I read the measurements to see where it really sits.

scenes.credit: Google's launch blog, the Gemini 4 family card

steps.say: On Google's own card, Neon is the middle model. Cheaper per token than Carbon, slower than Hydrogen.

steps.caption: $3 in, $15 out, per million tokens
steps.say: Three dollars in and fifteen out, per million tokens, with no surcharge for long context.

scenes.title: AA Intelligence Index, best level
scenes.note: Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon
scenes.say: But on Artificial Analysis's index, Neon at its top level scores above Carbon at its top level. The model card says Neon is adapted from Carbon. The child outscores the parent.

scenes.title: Why an agent's bill is mostly input

steps.say: An agent works in steps. On every step it sends the whole conversation so far, and writes a little more.
steps.term: Index task: one agent job in AA's index

steps.say: Most of what each step reads, it has read before. That comes from the cache at a twentieth of the price.
Only the new slice is billed at the full input rate.
Add it up for Neon at xhigh. Two sixty-six of full-rate input, one sixty-six of cache reads, two twelve of output. About two thirds of the bill is input.
Against Carbon, Neon wins on cost at every level. At the defaults it is forty-three percent cheaper per task.
GPT-6.2 Astra is the comparison Google left out. At xhigh it scores higher than Neon, for two fifty-two a task.

scenes.credit: Google's launch blog, cost per task chart

steps.say: Google's blog claims thirty-six percent less per task than competing models at their highest setting.

steps.caption: $6.44 against Opus 5.5's $10.04
steps.say: That is exactly Claude Opus five point five. Against both GPT-6.2 models, Neon costs more.

scenes.title: Coding Agent Index, mean cost per task
scenes.say: Fast end to end shows up in AA's coding agent runs. Three models tie on score. Neon does it for less than half Fable's money, in a bit over half the time.

scenes.credit: Parallel's search leaderboard, from its post on X

steps.say: The post calling Neon the highest-performing model measured is Parallel's web search board.

steps.caption: 88.13 against 86.94, about 100 tasks a suite
steps.say: Its lead is about a point, inside the noise, and Neon ran at high effort while Fable ran at max.

items.say: Third on the index is by model. By variant it is sixth.
On AA's meter, Neon at its top level guesses more often than the other Gemini 4 models at theirs.

items.text: Carbon medium is cheaper to Nov 30
items.say: And until November thirtieth, Carbon at medium costs less per task than Neon at high.

scenes.text: Between Carbon and Hydrogen on price. On the index, the best Gemini there is.
scenes.say: Between Carbon and Hydrogen is Google's price list talking. On the index, Neon is the best Gemini there is.

recap: about two thirds of the bill is input
scenes.say: Adapted from Carbon, scored over it, and cheapest where agents run long. Thanks for watching!
